what: Enterprise Products Partners owns midstream energy infrastructure: pipelines, storage, processing plants and export terminals, mainly for natural gas liquids, crude oil and petrochemicals along the US Gulf Coast.
customers: Oil and gas producers, refiners, petrochemical plants and export buyers in Asia and Europe.
money: natural gas liquids pipelines, fractionation and export
propylene, octane and refined product logistics
moat: An integrated network from Permian wellhead to Gulf Coast export dock, with assets that cannot be rebuilt and contracts of ten years or more.
risks: Debt of about $34 billion against almost no cash
Volumes depend on US drilling activity
It is a partnership, which complicates tax reporting for some investors
Revenue has drifted down about 3% a year over three years as commodity prices fell
opportunities: A distribution yield above 6%, raised every year for more than 25 years
Natural gas liquids exports to Asia keep growing
Petrochemical demand supports fractionation volumes regardless of oil prices
watch: Distributable cash flow coverage and new export capacity coming online.
